_doc: Kanto overworld placement for the FireRed/LeafGreen prototype (converter/frlg_plan.py plans -> b2tools/kanto_world.py). Parallel to data/hoenn_world.json + data/hoenn_world_layout.json but carrying only Kanto maps, so Hoenn's world build is untouched. 'layout' is each map's (tile_x, tile_z) on the global tile grid (top-left origin, tiles); placement is derived from the maps' own connections: Route 1 (24x40) sits north of Pallet Town (24x20) sharing x (Route1.down <-> PalletTown.up, offset 0); Viridian City (48x40) sits north of Route 1 (Route1.up <-> ViridianCity.down, offset -12 from Route 1 / +12 from Viridian); Route 2 (24x80) sits north of Viridian (ViridianCity.up <-> Route2.down, offset +12 / -12); Route 22 (48x24) sits west of Viridian (ViridianCity.left <-> Route22.right, offset +10 / -10). The whole web is shifted so every tile coordinate stays non-negative (Route 2 top at z=0, Route 22 left at x=0): Route 2 (60,0), Route 22 (0,90), Viridian (48,80), Route 1 (60,120), Pallet Town (60,160). 'maps' holds per-map Black 2 settings. margin_cells mirrors world.py's compose() one-cell forest ring.
_ids_doc: matrix/area/first_chunk and each map's 'zone' are the ROM-integration ids patches/kanto_world.py writes into the FireRedHD build (a/0/0/9 matrix index, the a/0/0/8 chunk the first Kanto cell becomes, a/0/1/3 area record, and the zone-header slots Pallet Town / Route 1 take). These are FireRedHD's region-base ids, measured off the shared Black 2 (pokebw2 b2_us) base that the FireRedHD NDS build starts from: a/0/0/8 has 1065 chunks and a/0/0/9 has 416 matrices of its own, so the first Kanto chunk is 1065 and the Kanto matrix is 416 (Kanto appends on Unova's own base, exactly as Hoenn did: same region-base numbers in data/hoenn_world.json). Zone slots 450/451/452/453/454 are free Unova headers (Black 2 has 615) that FireRedHD does not otherwise use; Pallet Town takes 450, Route 1 takes 451, Viridian City takes 452, Route 2 takes 453, Route 22 takes 454. 'buildings'/'signs'/'npcs'/'warps' are per-map model/event tables keyed by destination or script that world.map_events reads. 'buildings' names a Black 2 native exterior model per warp destination (res 0 = pc_01 Pokemon Center, res 2 = t2_house01 house, res 3 = t2_build01 Mart; the Kanto build runs no area2_buildings patch so only Black 2's own pack-0 models resolve) and map_events places it on the footprint, where kanto_features suppresses its placeholder box; 'front' is the model's depth in 16ths of a tile (Hoenn's validated value for that res). 'signs'/'npcs'/'warps' stay empty: the overworld builds with terrain + walkability + a fly point but no wired doors/NPCs yet (Kanto interiors and scripts come later).
